rules.description: Use guide plan, update, and next as durable recommendations; select only the workflow depth justified by risk and do not manufacture evidence for bypassed optional nodes.
Every feature task records its objective, scope, non-goals, acceptance, and the decision that starts the task before map inspection.

Every feature task reads the selected project's resource, function, mainline, module, and verification maps before source implementation; use the declared v3 function and verification map paths when that project owns them.
Source changes occur only after requirements and map_check, through the unique mapped owner in one clean owner worktree.
A source change is not delivered until an exact candidate is created and bound to its source tree and change set.
Every candidate runs the focused tests and gates required by its mapped feature; runtime changes use the real entrypoint when available.
Review is required before merge or push and must inspect the unchanged validated candidate and its map boundaries.
A task that enters mainline performs exact latest-main integration and records the resulting mainline identity.
Every task closes its own records, releases its own claim, and leaves only its own clean owner worktree removed after required delivery receipts.
Architecture may be bypassed after map_check when an existing design covers a small change; record the bypass decision.
Map update may be bypassed only when feature, owner, path, and gate bindings are unchanged; otherwise update the owning map source.
Effectiveness may be bypassed for non-runtime or low-risk changes; runtime and higher-risk changes replay it before integration.
Promotion may be bypassed when immutable Active/Protected delivery is not part of the task; cleanup remains mandatory.
Every debug task must bind the issue to the real function-map owner and required verification gates before implementation.
Every meaningful debug exploration, experiment, first divergence, causal result, and falsification is appended to the current worker run notes.
If the function map or gate binding is missing, record the gap and repair the declaration through its unique owner after the fix.
Root Guidance records cross-project relationships; implementation changes use the selected child's unique owner and adjacent mainline edge.
Debug resolve fixes the mapped unique owner, adds necessary regression coverage, and updates a function map or verification gate when the verified contract changes.
Before cleanup, reread project AGENTS.md, local Skills, and MEMORY.md; retain only verified reusable facts and promote rules to the owning file.
A project absent from the current root baseline, including agent-memory, remains pending and cannot be treated as an active path or source owner.
Read and apply only rule sources declared by the root project contract and the selected child project contract; do not infer an undeclared rule source from another project.
Prefer adjacent workflow transitions; skip only non-applicable detail through an explicit risk-based decision and retain the mandatory spine.
A passing required step must bind its real evidence; do not use a test, note, or generated placeholder as evidence for a different lifecycle level.
Revise the active plan through AppSDK when project, goal, source, scope, owner, rule context, gate, dependency, or environment changes.
Do not overwrite or delete PlanRevision records, execution events, child lifecycle records, or historical evidence to make a gate pass.
Do not claim lifecycle completion before the canonical AppSDK gates and the evidence required for that claim pass.
Locate every feature or debug request in the applicable root and child function maps and verification maps before recommending implementation.
During debug exploration, append observations, hypotheses, experiments, first divergence, and evidence to the active worker run notes before resolve.
When a verified change alters an owner, path, resource relation, mainline edge, or regression gate, update every affected owning declaration in the same change scope.

Routing, retry, provider selection, lifecycle, debug, environment, snapshot, and governance truth uses typed control resources, error chains, declared configuration, or records; it never enters business payloads, metadata, logs, or implicit context.
Each feature and semantic function has one mapped owner and one implementation; no duplicate path, reroute, fallback, silent downgrade, or dual implementation may be introduced.
Before adding behavior, confirm it is necessary and not already provided; prefer declared operation, hook, gate, or shared-function configuration over inline branching and duplicate helpers.

Review must block new violations of control separation, unique ownership, fallback prohibition, ablation, configuration-first design, or shared-function reuse; untouched historical violations are advisory unless they affect the changed boundary or evidence truth.

For a new, cross-project, or semantically significant feature, record requirements, architecture boundaries, and detailed design before implementation; a small covered change records an explicit architecture bypass.
Before repeating exploration or a failed command, inspect prior verified successes, failures, run notes, and retry permission; do not retry an unchanged failure.

nodes.instruction: Record objective, scope, non-goals, acceptance, and the one-line decision for this feature task.
Read the selected project's actual resource, function, mainline, module, and verification maps before implementation.
Optionally close top-down boundaries and design when the existing maps/design do not cover the change.
Change only the mapped unique owner in the clean owner worktree.
Create and bind the exact candidate source tree and change set before delivery.
Run the mapped focused tests and gates, plus real entrypoint checks for runtime-visible changes.
Update the owning function, mainline, resource, or verification map when the feature, owner, path, or gate binding changed.
Pass review on the unchanged validated candidate before merge or push.
Optionally replay effectiveness without changing the reviewed source; select it for runtime or higher-risk work.
Integrate the exact candidate on latest main and verify the resulting mainline identity when mainline delivery is requested.
Optionally publish immutable Active and retain Protected history when the task requires promotion.
Close the task, review AGENTS/Skills/MEMORY, release the own claim, and remove only the own clean worktree after required receipts.

workflows.objective: Deliver a feature through the mandatory governance spine while recording explicit risk-based bypasses.

nodes.instruction: Read AGENTS, existing notes and records, the resource/function/mainline/module maps, and verification gates; bind the issue and owner.
Reproduce where feasible, keep one hypothesis, record each meaningful experiment and first divergence in the worker run notes.
Fix the unique mapped owner, add needed regression coverage, and update maps or gates when the verified contract changes.
Create and bind the exact fix candidate before delivery.
Run focused regression/gates and the original or equivalent real entrypoint replay.
Pass review on the unchanged validated fix candidate before merge or push.
Integrate the exact fix on latest main and verify mainline identity when mainline delivery is requested.
Review AGENTS/Skills/MEMORY, close the task, release the own claim, and remove only the own clean worktree after required receipts.

workflows.objective: Resolve a defect from mapped context and recorded exploration through an evidence-backed delivery path.

nodes.instruction: Inspect the repository root, child projects, AppSDK state, maps, records, and retained history; define scope and protected boundaries.
Initialize only approved root Guidance sources through the official AppSDK flow; preserve child contracts and lifecycle truth.
Run local AppSDK baseline verification and compile, and record root Guidance state separately from child lifecycle claims.

workflows.objective: Enter root Guidance without destroying existing child-project truth.

nodes.instruction: Inspect project version, migration records, staging, maps, locks, Active, Protected, and historical evidence without editing them.
Select the official compatible migration or explicitly authorized fresh initialization route; identify canonical owner, preserved truth, reversible boundary, and retry permission.
Execute the selected AppSDK route once, retaining immutable history and never hand-writing migration records, hashes, receipts, or timestamps.
Verify the migrated root contract, maps, lock, records, and child-project boundaries; do not treat a partial or failed transaction as success.

workflows.objective: Reconcile or reset legacy root governance only through an explicit, auditable AppSDK route.

nodes.instruction: Record objective, scope, non-goals, acceptance, risk, and the selected child project without guessing a missing project or module.
Read resources first, then function, mainline, module, and verification maps; bind the unique owner and adjacent edges or record the missing-map gap.
Declare one clean owner worktree from latest origin/main and preserve main, other workers, child records, and protected state.
Run applicable local AppSDK and project preflight gates before implementation; revise the plan if bound context changed.

workflows.objective: Bind a task to its goal, project, module, owner, maps, worktree, and required gates before code work.

nodes.instruction: Pass local AppSDK review admission for the exact candidate, required evidence set, and current map context.

Run the configured read-only review route and inspect control separation, unique owner, no fallback, ablation, configuration-first operations/hooks, shared functions, and explicit missing capability behavior; new violations block and untouched historical violations are advisory.
Replay required effectiveness without changing the reviewed source, candidate, artifact, or environment binding.

workflows.objective: Admit and review the exact evidence-bound candidate without source drift.

nodes.instruction: Run project-owned internal validation against the exact candidate and retain failure evidence.
Build the exact candidate artifact from the bound source tree and declared environment.
Install the exact artifact into the declared user-facing environment and retain the install receipt.
Restart the declared runtime when required and retain the restart receipt.
Replay the real public deployed entrypoint and retain observable success or failure evidence.
Bind whitebox, artifact, install, restart, and blackbox evidence to the same candidate, source tree, environment, entrypoint, and input.

workflows.objective: Prove a runtime candidate through its real deployed entrypoint when delivery is in scope.

nodes.instruction: Fetch latest origin/main and refresh the integration base without mutating main or another worker's dirty worktree.
Verify the exact integrated tree and affected project gates before merge or push.
Merge and push only the reviewed, validated candidate through the protected mainline route.
Observe the remote main ref and bind a receipt to the exact pushed commit.

workflows.objective: Merge only an exact candidate verified against the latest mainline.

nodes.instruction: Run and bind the required merged-source regression suite.
Compile the canonical merged project artifact and retain its generated evidence.
Publish the immutable Active artifact while retaining Protected history.

workflows.objective: Turn verified mainline source into immutable consumable output when promotion is required.

nodes.instruction: Create the canonical Protected archive through AppSDK, preserving prior immutable history.
Bind source, artifact, API, regression, promotion, and remote truth through the canonical producer.
Verify Active and Protected immutability without changing frozen hashes or records.

workflows.objective: Protect the exact published source, contracts, and artifact when freeze is required.

nodes.instruction: Record retained evidence, preserved history, and disposable state; verify the task is eligible for cleanup.
Remove only the merged, clean owner worktree and branch after remote receipt; never remove another worker's or dirty path.
Release the task claim only after worktree removal and its verification are recorded.

workflows.objective: Release only resources whose delivery, retention, and remote evidence are complete.
